newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift, interest seen on second tier.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift, interest seen on second tier.

text.p: Leading Russian shares ended barely changed in lethargic trading on Thursday, traders said, citing an almost total absence of demand on the threshold of August's traditional holiday exodus.

The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at 506.45, slightly lower than Wednesday's closing 508.12. But it had barely moved from the trading session's opening 506.63. Total market turnover was an uninspiring $52.2 million.
"We spent the whole day today hovering around one to two percent change," said Trinfiko's senior trader Grigory Pinsky. "Shares passed from dealer to dealer."

Traders said interest was greater in the less liquid second-tier stock, and United City Bank head of securities Samit Yakovlev noted a rise in Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS preferred shares, the only major movement of the trading session, he said.
Trading was on speculation that a forthcoming sale of 38 percent of the metals producer would open the door for some preferred stock to be converted to ordinary stock, he said.
Preferred shares NKEL_p.RTS rose to $13.50 from $12.10, while ordinary shares NKEL.RTS rose to $15.3 from $14.90.
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.4190 from $0.4150.
"No-one is buying UES shares," said Yakovlev. "Clients basically aren't buying any blue chips."

Moscow-based investment bank Renaissance Capital announced after market close that it and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were awarded a mandate to lead-manage UES's Eurobond placement, which it said would be at least $200 million.
